subject.title: fix(skills): enforce byte-level cap on skill package downloads

question: Should OpenClaw enforce one download-size policy across ClawHub package fetches and skill dependency installers, and what explicit override should preserve legitimate oversized artifacts?
rationale: The patch selects a permanent 256 MiB security and compatibility boundary from skill-source classification, but source location neither covers the stated ClawHub fetch path nor reliably represents download trust.

options.title: Protect both download flows
options.body: Move byte accounting into the relevant shared download primitives and require explicit confirmation or an existing break-glass mechanism for oversized artifacts.

options.title: Narrow this PR's contract
options.body: Limit this PR to gateway dependency-installer hardening, retitle and document that scope, and track ClawHub package limits separately before claiming registry protection.

options.title: Keep source-scoped behavior
options.body: Accept the 256 MiB managed-source rule and its uncovered workspace and ClawHub paths as an intentionally partial mitigation.

recommendation.title: Protect both download flows
recommendation.body: Move byte accounting into the relevant shared download primitives and require explicit confirmation or an existing break-glass mechanism for oversized artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline already routed the compatibility and security-boundary decision to this repository owner.
